slide.title: Hand-off That Really Arrives
slide.body: Chat bubble → folded summary note → inbox with a person icon, connected by a teal path. Small tag: AI for Customer Experience and Support · Lesson 10 · Capstone step 2.

scenes.on_screen_text: From paper rules to a real person
scenes.voiceover: In lesson seven, you wrote hand-off rules on paper. Today you connect them to a place where a real person will see them, and you make sure the customer knows exactly what happens next.

slide.title: Adding the Hand-off Flow
slide.body: AI for Customer Experience and Support · Lesson 10 of 12 · Capstone step 2

scenes.voiceover: This is capstone step two. Your assistant from the last lesson answers questions. Now it needs a hand-off flow, and every hand-off flow has four parts: trigger, collect, send and tell.

slide.title: The four-part flow: 1 and 2
slide.body: Four boxes in a row, first two highlighted: 1. Trigger (asks for a person · very upset · refund above limit · legal or safety · sensitive topic · fails twice) → 2. Collect (email, order number, permission to share) → 3. Send → 4. Tell

scenes.voiceover: Trigger means the rules that start the hand-off, such as a request for a person, a very upset customer, a refund above your limit, or a safety issue. Collect means what the assistant asks first. Only what is needed, such as an email address, and permission to share the conversation.

slide.title: The four-part flow: 3 and 4
slide.body: Same four boxes, last two highlighted: 3. Send (email inbox · help desk ticket · team chat channel) → 4. Tell (who, which channel, when).

scenes.voiceover: Send means where the summary goes: an email inbox, a help desk ticket, or a team chat channel. Tell means what the customer sees: who will reply, through which channel, and when.

slide.title: Two ways to send
slide.body: Option A: the builder's own hand-off or email notification. Option B: builder sends data out → n8n or Zapier → email + row in a sheet. Banner: choose the simplest option that works.

scenes.voiceover: There are two common ways to send the summary. Many chatbot builders have their own hand-off or email notification feature. Or, if the builder can send data out, an automation in n8n or Zapier can email the team or add a row to a sheet, as in lesson eight. Choose the simplest option that works on your plan.

slide.title: Tell the customer
slide.body: Weak (grey): 'Your request has been escalated.' Strong (teal): 'I have passed your question to our support team, with a summary of our chat. A person will reply by email within one working day.'

scenes.voiceover: The final message must be honest and specific. Your request has been escalated, is weak. Compare this. I have passed your question to our support team, with a summary of our chat. A person will reply by email within one working day. Only promise times your team can meet.

scenes.stock_query: hotel receptionist writing a message note
scenes.on_screen_text: A note on the wrong desk
scenes.voiceover: Think of leaving a message at a hotel reception. A good receptionist writes who called, why and how to reply, puts the note in the right box, and tells the caller when the guest will get it. A note on the wrong desk is no message at all.

scenes.stock_query: safari vehicle on savanna at sunrise
scenes.voiceover: Let's build it. Wanjiru manages customer service for a hypothetical safari travel company in Nairobi, Kenya. Her assistant answers questions about trip dates, packing and payment, often when the office is closed.

screen_steps: Open the test bot in Botpress and go to the human hand-off (HITL) settings
Add trigger phrases and topics: 'person', 'agent', 'change my booking', 'injured', 'medical'
Show the list of triggers saved
scenes.voiceover: In the chatbot builder, I open the hand-off settings. I add the triggers from lesson seven: person, agent, change my booking, injured and medical. So a request for a person, a booking change, or a safety or medical issue will hand off.

screen_steps: In the hand-off step, add the question: 'May I have your email address so a colleague can reply? I will share a summary of our chat with them.'
Add the summary fields: Need, Trigger, Details, Assistant said, Mood, Urgency
scenes.voiceover: Next, collect. The assistant asks: may I have your email address, so a colleague can reply? I will share a summary of our chat with them. Then I set the summary fields from the template: need, trigger, details, what the assistant said, mood and urgency.

screen_steps: Option A (record): choose the builder's email notification and enter the test support inbox address
Option B (optional insert, only if confirmed): send the hand-off to a Zapier or n8n automation that emails the team and adds a row to a 'Hand-offs' sheet
scenes.voiceover: Now, send. The simplest option is the builder's own email notification, going to a test support inbox. If your builder can send data out, you could instead pass the hand-off to Zapier or n8n, to email the team and log it in a hand-offs sheet.

screen_steps: Type: 'Our team is offline now. A person will read your message and reply by email when the office opens. For an emergency during your trip, use the emergency number in your travel documents.'
scenes.voiceover: Then, tell. For out of hours, I write: our team is offline now. A person will read your message and reply by email when the office opens. For an emergency during your trip, use the emergency number in your travel documents.

screen_steps: Open the 'Emulator' test chat and type a made-up request: 'I want to change my booking, can I talk to a person?'
Switch to the test inbox and open the summary; highlight the missing email field in red
Back in the builder, move the Collect step before the Send step
Retest and show the complete summary in the inbox
scenes.voiceover: Finally, I test with a made-up conversation, and check the inbox. The summary arrived, but without the customer's email. The assistant handed off before asking. So Wanjiru moves collect before send, and the retest is complete.

scenes.on_screen_text: Test until a person sees it
scenes.voiceover: A common mistake is to see the confirmation message in the chat and assume it works. The summary may go to an old inbox nobody reads. Always test the full path, until a person sees the summary.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. Trigger → collect → send → tell. 2. A real human channel; the simplest option that works. 3. Who, how, when; test the full path.

scenes.voiceover: Let's recap. First, a hand-off flow has four parts: trigger, collect, send and tell. Second, connect it to a real human channel, with the builder's own feature or an automation, and choose the simplest option. Third, tell customers who will reply, how and when, and test the full path.

This is capstone step two. In the exercise, you will fill in the four-part template, add at least four triggers, and connect your hand-off to a test inbox or sheet. Then test three made-up conversations. In the next lesson, we look at testing your assistant for accuracy, tone and safety. See you there.
